deep.heading: The order a build really runs in
deep.body: Every build follows the same chain. The paint is loaded, then the Recolor source paint sliders (Hue, Sat, Bright) are applied, then Auto-levels if ticked, then the look itself is sculpted (Scratch, Catalog, Fusion, FRACTURE or CANDY DEPTH). After that come the Channel trims, then the protection map for decals with its Feather and Decal finish, then any Detail bake, and last the safety pass that keeps the map legal for iRacing. Because the recolor happens first, the paint copy written beside the spec is the recolored one, not your original. The live preview runs the same chain at 512 and 1024 pixels; Generate runs it at the full 2048.

deep.heading: What lands on disk and what it is called
deep.body: A build writes two files into a job folder: your paint and the spec map. The spec is named car_spec followed by your member ID. The paint copy is named car_num followed by the ID when Custom-number car is ticked (it is ticked by default), or car followed by the ID when you untick it for a number that the sim stamps itself. That is why the member ID is required: it is part of the name iRacing looks for. Simple mode refuses any source that is not exactly 2048 by 2048. Advanced only refuses when you tick Reject unless source is exactly 2048x2048; otherwise it resizes and shows a warning. The lab keeps the newest 10 jobs.

settings.Source image: Drop a 2048 x 2048 TGA, PNG, JPEG or PSD
settings.Style Gallery: tap one of the 12 go-to styles

examples.result: The paint and spec files are written to the job folder and copied to the car you picked; refresh the car in iRacing to see it.

examples.goal: Start without knowing any material names.
examples.result: Auto-Sculpt reads the paint, picks a best-fit look and shows what it chose, so the choice teaches you which family suits your livery.

combos.why: Start there for the plain meaning of the red, green and blue channels this lab writes.
The safety pass at the end of every build enforces exactly these rules, so a Spec Sculpt map never breaks them.
Covers the deploy side: member ID, car folder, Live Link and Deploy last job.
Shows where to find your member ID and how car folders are matched.

faq.q: Does Spec Sculpt change my paint colors?
faq.a: No, it writes the spec map. The only way the paint copy changes is if you move the Recolor source paint sliders (Hue, Sat, Bright), because the recolor is applied before sculpting and the recolored paint is what is saved.

faq.q: Do I need my member ID just to preview?
faq.a: No. The ID only sets the file name used when a job is written and deployed, so previews and variations work without it.

faq.q: Why does Simple mode refuse my image?
faq.a: Simple requires an exactly 2048 x 2048 iRacing template. Advanced can resize on purpose, or reject non-2048 sources if you tick the strict option.

faq.q: How is this different from the main Paint Booth?
faq.a: The booth paints colour and finish zone by zone and renders both. Spec Sculpt starts from a finished paint and only writes how that paint catches light.

mistakes.symptom: Simple mode rejects the file or the build stops straight away.
mistakes.cause: The source is not exactly 2048 x 2048, and Simple always applies the strict check.
mistakes.fix: Export the paint at 2048 x 2048, or switch View to Advanced and leave the strict box unticked to allow a deliberate resize.

mistakes.symptom: The preview looks great but the car in iRacing shows nothing new.
mistakes.cause: The job was built but never deployed, or the member ID or car folder was wrong, so the file name did not match.
mistakes.fix: Check the member ID, pick the car from Deploy to, build with BUILD + INSTALL IN iRACING (or Deploy last job), then refresh the car in iRacing.

mistakes.symptom: The spec fits a different colour than the paint you exported.
mistakes.cause: Recolor source paint was left moved, so the sculpt and the saved paint copy use the shifted colours.
mistakes.fix: Press Reset next to the Recolor source paint sliders before the final build.

protips: Untick Custom-number car only when you let iRacing stamp the number: the paint copy then uses the plain car name instead of car_num, and the sim adds the number itself.
The live preview is a quick 512 pass and the final is 2048. Judge fine detail on the final build, not on the small preview.

deep.heading: How Fusion splits the final mix
deep.body: Fusion has one main knob, Mix weight toward catalog, which starts at 50%. At 71% the catalog picks supply about 71% of the final blend and the library looks share the other 29%. Under the hood every pick is a real Paint Booth finish; the engine adds up the weights of all picks, keeps the 5 heaviest, and renormalises them so only the ratio matters. So adding a sixth finish drops the lightest one rather than diluting the rest. Scratch with no catalog picks uses just the library stack, and Catalog with no library picks uses just your catalog finishes.

deep.heading: Balanced versus Showroom, as written
deep.body: Balanced is a plain weighted average per channel. Showroom changes only metal: it takes the larger of the two weighted contributions instead of adding them, while roughness and clearcoat stay a straight average. With two equally metallic sources at a 50% mix, Balanced keeps the full metal value but Showroom keeps half of it, so Showroom does not make a mid mix shinier. In the current build the single mix weight is what clearly moves a Fusion built from library looks, so judge Mix strategy and the per-channel split by eye with Compare Looks rather than assuming they act.

deep.heading: FRACTURE and CANDY DEPTH are builders of their own
deep.body: These two sit beside the modes but run their own sculpt and their own sliders. FRACTURE: Ignition 0 to 2, Angle gate 0.25 to 2, Trace strength 0 to 2 (each starts at 1.00), Calm floor 14 to 110 (starts at 30; lower is a glossier mirror body) and Decorrelation 0 to 1 (starts at 0). CANDY DEPTH: Depth 0 to 1.5 (1.00), Flake density 0 to 1 (0.50), Flake size 0.5 to 3 pixels (1.0), Wetness 0 to 1 (0.78) and Satin floor 0.15 to 0.8 (0.42). Both leave the paint untouched. Batch Sculpt a Folder cannot run them and falls back to Scratch.

examples.title: Chrome with a carbon accent in Fusion
examples.goal: Mix a real catalog material with a library look.
examples.result: About 71% of the blend comes from the catalog carbon finish and the rest from Mirror Chrome, so the car reads mostly carbon with chrome in the lighter areas.

examples.title: Glossier FRACTURE body
examples.goal: Make the mirror body of FRACTURE cleaner and sharper.
examples.result: Lanes become sharper, quiet areas get glossier, and metal, roughness and clearcoat patterns stop being carbon copies of each other.

examples.title: Deep wet candy with visible flake
examples.goal: A bottomless candy coat with flakes that read through it.
examples.result: Rich and dark areas become deep glassy pools while pale areas stay thin satin, with flakes suspended in the coat.

combos.why: Scratch and the library side of Fusion both draw from the 125 presets.
Paint response applies to every mode, so you can steer where a Fusion lands on the car.
Spec strength and the Channel trims are the quickest way to rebalance a Fusion after mixing.
Catalog mode borrows these real finishes, so browsing the catalogue shows what you can pick.

faq.q: Which mode should I start with?
faq.a: Scratch. The library looks are already real finishes, so it is the quickest route to a believable result. Move to Fusion when you want a specific catalog material in the mix.

faq.q: Why can I only blend 5 things?
faq.a: The engine keeps the 5 heaviest finishes and drops the rest, and the library stack itself is limited to 5 looks.

faq.q: Does FRACTURE change my paint?
faq.a: No. FRACTURE and CANDY DEPTH only sculpt the spec; the paint stays as it is.

faq.q: Can I batch FRACTURE across a folder?
faq.a: Not directly. Batch Sculpt a Folder falls back to Scratch for Fusion, candy and fracture looks.

mistakes.symptom: Fusion at 50% looks duller in metal than either source alone.
mistakes.cause: Showroom keeps only the larger weighted contribution, so equal sources give half the metal at a 50% mix.
mistakes.fix: Switch Mix strategy to Balanced, push the mix weight toward the shinier side, or raise the M channel trim.

mistakes.symptom: Moving the Mix weight does nothing.
mistakes.cause: Only one side has picks, so there is nothing to mix: Catalog needs a ticked catalog finish and Scratch needs a library look.
mistakes.fix: Tick at least one catalog finish and one library look in Fusion.

mistakes.symptom: A sixth pick seems to have no effect.
mistakes.cause: Only the 5 heaviest finishes are blended; the lightest are dropped.
mistakes.fix: Raise the weight of the one you care about or remove a weaker pick.

protips: The FRACTURED colour-shift styles in the Style Gallery key off paint brightness. If one looks flat, open Recolor source paint and lift Bright, then build again.
In Fusion you can read the exact share on screen: the hint under the Mix weight says 71% means the catalog is about 71% and the scratch stack shares the other 29%.
Use Compare Looks (4 slots) to settle Balanced versus Showroom on your own paint instead of trusting a rule of thumb.

deep.heading: A preset is a recipe of real finishes
deep.body: Every one of the 125 presets points at one or a few real Paint Booth finishes, each with its own weight. The six groups hold Candy and pearl 22, Holo and shift 22, Chrome and metal 21, Carbon and matte 20, Flake and sparkle 20 and Exotic and glow 20. When you stack up to 5 looks, their finishes are merged, the 5 heaviest are kept and the weights are renormalised, so you set ratios, not absolute amounts. Presets are no longer procedural guesses: the lab switched to real finishes after the procedural versions came out too samey.

deep.heading: Why 22 presets are built finer
deep.body: A finish always has the same number of cells whether it is drawn on a thumbnail or a whole car, so a coarse one looks huge on a 2048 body. After the owner audit, 22 presets are flagged too big and are rendered at half size and mirror-tiled up 2 times, which makes their pattern twice as fine and keeps it seamless. They include Hex Flake, Organic Flake Cells and Chrome Mosaic. Everything else renders at normal scale. Cultural and illustrative finishes translate poorly into a spec map, so the library favours material families such as chrome, pearl, brushed and carbon.

examples.result: Builds a stack of candy, pearl and a chrome outline in one click; the stack bar shows each layer and its share.

settings.Weights: lower Mirror Chrome until the stack bar shows it as the smaller share

examples.result: Directional brushed bands carry the body while the chrome adds clean highlights; this is the pair the Brushed Metal auto look uses.

examples.result: Frozen matte plus silk matte: both low-gloss, so the car reads flat without becoming one solid grey.

combos.why: Fusion mixes this library with real catalog finishes.
Favorites, Recent and Compare Looks keep the stacks you like within reach.
Five tested starting stacks built from these presets.
Explains how preset feels map to spec behaviour in the main booth.

faq.q: How many looks can I stack?
faq.a: Up to 5. The engine also keeps at most 5 finishes in the final blend.

faq.q: Why are only some styles shown in Simple mode?
faq.a: Simple shows 12 go-to styles for speed. Advanced reveals 60 and more one-click styles plus the full library with search and groups.

faq.q: What do the weights mean?
faq.a: They are relative. The engine renormalises them, so doubling every weight changes nothing; only the ratio between looks counts.

faq.q: Can I find a preset by what it does?
faq.a: Yes. The filter matches names and tags, so words such as chrome, mercury, brushed or flake work.

mistakes.symptom: A big flake or mosaic look reads huge and blobby on the car.
mistakes.cause: Its cells are coarse at whole-car scale; only the 22 audited presets are tiled finer.
mistakes.fix: Pick a finer relative from the same group, or stack it under a finer look at a small weight.

mistakes.symptom: The stack of five looks all blur into one grey result.
mistakes.cause: Equal weights across many different looks average out their character.
mistakes.fix: Give one look the lead weight, keep the others as small accents, or drop to two or three layers.

mistakes.symptom: The cultural or illustrative finish I wanted barely shows.
mistakes.cause: Illustration-style finishes carry their look in the paint, not in the spec map.
mistakes.fix: Choose a material family (chrome, pearl, brushed, carbon) and let the paint carry the artwork.

protips: Auto-Sculpt ranks 7 ready-made pairs against your paint: Chrome Depth, Candy Show, Dark Satin, Brushed Metal, Anodized Gloss, Machined Graphic and Flake Pop. Another Smart Look walks down that ranking.
Star a preset with the Favorites toggle and it floats into a pinned Favorites rail, so your go-to looks are one tap away on every livery.

deep.heading: What the emphasis really multiplies
deep.body: Paint response changes metal and clearcoat only, never roughness. It first scores every pixel from 0 to 1 using your own paint as the yardstick, so it works on dark and bright liveries alike: Bright uses the 35th to 92nd brightness percentile, Dark the 8th to 65th, and Saturated and Muted use saturation percentiles (30th to 95th and 5th to 70th). A near-grey paint has no saturation to read, so those two fall back to brightness. The gain is 1 plus strength times (score minus 0.35) times 1.35, held between 0.52 and 1.62, and a small additive nudge makes sure the paint still shows through finishes with strong patterns of their own.

deep.heading: Hue boost and the hidden seed emphasis
deep.body: Hue boost builds a bell-shaped match around your colour; the Hue match width (20 to 120 degrees, default 60) sets its spread, and the match is weaker on dark or grey pixels. Its gain is held between 0.55 and 1.65 and strength runs 0 to 100. One surprise: with the menu on Uniform and strength at 0, the engine still applies a gentle emphasis of 0.5 chosen from your Seed, cycling Bright, Saturated, Dark, Bright, Muted. So changing the seed also moves where the paint shows through. The one-pass quick build used by Simple mode and guided Auto-Sculpt skips this step; Advanced builds use it.

examples.title: Chrome only on the bright graphics
examples.goal: Let the light parts of the livery carry the shine.
examples.result: Metal and clearcoat rise on light areas and ease off on dark ones, so graphics glow while dark body panels stay calmer.

examples.title: Make just the reds glossier
examples.goal: Target one colour of the livery.
examples.result: Pixels near that red get more metal and clearcoat with a soft falloff, while other colours keep the look as it was.

combos.why: Spec strength and Channel trims then rescale the whole map after emphasis has shaped it.
Paint response is the lab version of making the spec follow what the paint is doing.
Putting shine on the complementary or contrasting parts is what makes a finish pop.
Eyedropper, Color to Material and Tone to Material are the hands-on versions of the same idea.

faq.q: Does it change roughness too?
faq.a: No. The emphasis scales the metal and clearcoat channels only; roughness comes from the look you picked.

faq.q: Why does the result change when I only change the seed?
faq.a: With Uniform and strength 0 the engine still applies a mild emphasis picked from the seed. Set an explicit emphasis to control it.

faq.q: What strength should I start with?
faq.a: Low. The strength runs 0 to 100 and starts at 0; a value around 40 is a clear but safe first step.

faq.q: It does nothing in Simple mode. Why?
faq.a: Simple uses the quick one-pass build, which skips Paint response. Switch View to Advanced.

mistakes.symptom: Hue boost does nothing on the colour I picked.
mistakes.cause: Hue boost strength still sits at its start value of 0, or the colour is very dark or grey on the car.
mistakes.fix: Raise Hue boost strength above 0 and widen the match width; sample the real colour with the Eyedropper.

mistakes.symptom: The whole car goes metallic at high strength.
mistakes.cause: The gain can reach 1.62 times on both metal and clearcoat, so a look that is already shiny runs out of headroom.
mistakes.fix: Lower Emphasis strength, or choose Dark or Muted to aim at the area you want to keep calm.

mistakes.symptom: Muted or Saturated looks identical on a black and white car.
mistakes.cause: A grey livery has no saturation spread, so the engine uses brightness instead.
mistakes.fix: Use Bright or Dark on grey paints.

protips: Because emphasis scales clearcoat as well as metal, Bright at low strength gives the sparkle-on-highlights look without touching how smooth the surface is.
Recolor source paint with Bright lifted is a cheap way to change what Bright emphasis catches, because the recolor runs before the sculpt.

deep.heading: Which DNA sliders act, and when
deep.body: Procedural detail intensity, Interior flatten and the three Void caps feed the paint-derived build, the one used when no look from the library or catalog is picked. When you pick a look, the engine builds from that finish and does not read Detail intensity or Interior flatten. In a full Advanced build a void clamp still runs at the standard values (metal at most 92, roughness at least 158, clearcoat at most 44), ignoring the three Void sliders, and it relaxes as the car gets dark: full strength until about 22% of the sheet is dark and flat, gone by about 55%. The quick build in Simple mode skips the clamp. Spec strength and Channel trims act in every mode.

deep.heading: Spec strength, trims and the safety pass
deep.body: Spec strength scales the metal channel, and the build limits the multiplier to between 0 and 100%. The slider runs to 200%, but values above 100% give the same result as 100%. To push a channel harder use Channel trims (M, R and Cc from 30 to 200, starting at 100): each trim multiplies its channel after the look is built, then values are clipped to 0 to 255. After the trims, the protection map and the Detail bake, the safety pass runs: clearcoat from 1 to 15 snaps to 0 below 8 and to 16 otherwise, roughness is lifted to 15 wherever metal is under 240, and if more than 55% of the car is mirror metal those pixels drop to 239.

deep.heading: Seed, Chromatic shift and Auto-levels
deep.body: Seed (default 9101) makes a build repeatable: the same paint, look and seed give the same map, and Random gives a new variation. The lab describes Chromatic shift (ticked by default) as affecting only the procedural scratch part, not library or catalog finishes. Auto-levels stretches each colour channel of the source paint between its 1st and 99th percentile before sculpting, which gives a washed-out paint more contrast to work with. If you tick Blend notes into variation, the text of Style notes is mixed into the seed, so the same paint with different notes diverges.

examples.title: Calmer, softer skin (no look picked)
examples.goal: Quiet a busy paint-derived build.
examples.result: Ridges and dots ease off and dark, low-detail pockets lean matte, so ink fields do not bloom metallic.

examples.title: Tame a runaway shine on any look
examples.goal: Bring metal and clearcoat down without changing the look.
examples.result: Metal reads duller everywhere and the coat eases slightly; the pattern of the look stays the same.

examples.title: Compare one change at a time
examples.goal: Judge a single tweak fairly.

settings.Compare Looks: Add current to compare before and after the tweak

examples.result: Because the seed is fixed, any difference between the two slots comes from the one setting you changed.

combos.why: Emphasis shapes where metal and clearcoat land; the DNA sliders then set how strong and how detailed the whole map is.
The safety pass at the end is these rules; DNA sliders can never push a build past them.
The Channel trims here work like the booth channel sliders: a gain on one channel of the finished map.
Read the false-colour composite to see what a DNA change did to metal, roughness and clearcoat.

faq.q: I moved Procedural detail intensity and nothing changed.
faq.a: A look is picked. The slider only feeds the paint-derived build used when no library or catalog look is selected. Clear your picks to see it work.

faq.q: What do the defaults look like in one line?
faq.a: Detail 1.59, Interior flatten 38%, Spec strength 100%, Void caps metal 92, roughness 158, clearcoat 44. The Reset advanced to defaults button restores them.

faq.q: Can I make the metal stronger than 100%?
faq.a: Not with Spec strength: the build limits it to 100%. Raise the M Channel trim instead, up to 200.

faq.q: What is the difference between the four DNA presets?
faq.a: Catalog signature is 1.59 with 38% flatten, Rich detail 1.78 with 36%, Softer 1.36 with 42% and Ink-heavy panels 1.52 with 44%.

mistakes.symptom: Spec strength at 150% looks the same as 100%.
mistakes.cause: The build limits the strength multiplier to 100%.
mistakes.fix: Leave Spec strength at 100% and use the M Channel trim for more metal.

mistakes.symptom: Void caps changes have no effect in a look-based build.
mistakes.cause: Picked looks use the standard void values, not the sliders, and Simple mode skips the clamp.
mistakes.fix: Judge voids by Interior flatten on a paint-derived build, or use Detail bake and trims on a look.

mistakes.symptom: Dark livery loses its matte pockets.
mistakes.cause: The void clamp relaxes as the dark share of the car rises, so dark cars keep each finish whole.
mistakes.fix: That is by design; use Region Brush with Matte on the areas that must stay flat.

protips: Detail intensity 1.59 is the same global setting the shipped finishes use, so leaving it alone keeps a paint-derived build consistent with the catalog.
Keep the seed fixed while you explore, and change it only when you want a fresh variation of a look you already like.

deep.heading: Where it stands in this build
deep.body: The flat-image splitter, with its Separate button and the Sensitivity (30 to 200, 1.0x) and Number size (40 to 250, 1.0x) sliders, is switched off in the current beta because its accuracy was not good enough to ship. The same goes for the Auto-build layers button in the booth. What works today is the PSD layer picker (all, none and invert, with Protect edge, Feather and Decal finish) and Auto-detect decals for flat paints. Everything below describes the engine that sits behind the switched-off splitter, so you know what it does and why it was held back.

deep.heading: How the splitter reasons
deep.body: It builds five masks that tile the car with no overlap: numbers, sponsors, car template, brand graphics and paint, where paint is simply everything left over. Text is read at four 90 degree turns so vertical sponsor names are caught, digits go to numbers and words to sponsors, taking about 13 seconds per livery on a normal computer. The car is identified by scoring the sheet against stored layouts of 67 known cars, mixing 45% brightness match with 55% panel-edge match (about 79% exact and 86% family accuracy). The fixed template is trusted only at 0.20 confidence or more, must match the car make, and is kept only if it covers between 0.2% and 10% of the sheet.

deep.heading: Why graphic logos were the weak spot
deep.body: A logo with no readable text cannot be found by the text reader, so it falls into paint and gets sculpted like the body. The detector for graphic logos is off by default and needs a component that the shipped app does not include. A separate research model on a GPU reached 85.7% of priority cars fully correct (24 of 28), but it is not part of the buyer app. A big number that the text reader misses is rescued only if it is three digits or fewer and read with at least 0.45 confidence, which is why mistakes lean toward missing a number rather than mislabelling a sponsor.

examples.title: Sculpt only the body of a layered PSD
examples.goal: Keep every decal layer untouched.

settings.PSD layers: click none, then tick only the body layers

examples.result: Ticked layers are sculpted; unticked layers stay flat with a satin finish so numbers and sponsors read as vinyl.

examples.title: Flat paint with no layers
examples.goal: Protect numbers and sponsors on a TGA without a PSD.

settings.Preview: click and check what is shielded

examples.result: The detector marks decals as protected so they stay flat while the body is sculpted; check the preview before building.

combos.why: The live way to protect decals on a flat paint while the splitter is off.
Explains why the booth side of Smart Separate is not loaded in this build.
Decal Rescue sets the spec under numbers and sponsors inside the booth when a decal arrives glossy.
A layered PSD gives the cleanest separation because the layers are already yours.

faq.q: Where is the Separate button?
faq.a: It is switched off in this beta build while accuracy is improved. Use a layered PSD or Auto-detect decals instead.

faq.q: Why does a graphic logo still get sculpted?
faq.a: Logos with no readable text are invisible to the text reader and fall into the paint mask. Check the protect preview and shield them with a PSD layer or the Region Brush.

faq.q: Does it work for every car?
faq.a: The fixed car template exists for 67 known cars only. Other cars still get numbers and sponsors but no template layer.

faq.q: What do the Decal finish options do?
faq.a: They set the flat look given to protected areas: Matte, Satin, Glossy, Wet or Carbon, from roughest to smoothest in the order Matte 160, Carbon 150, Satin 110, Glossy 45, Wet 35 (roughness).

mistakes.symptom: Looking for Separate or Auto-build layers and not finding them.
mistakes.cause: They are not loaded in the beta customer build.
mistakes.fix: Open a layered PSD, or tick Auto-detect decals under Advanced.

mistakes.symptom: Sponsor text is shielded as a number.
mistakes.cause: Number size treats tall glyphs as numbers, and big sponsor words can pass the height test.
mistakes.fix: Raise Number size where the splitter is available, or untick that layer in the PSD list.

mistakes.symptom: A template layer is missing on a car you know.
mistakes.cause: The match was below 0.20 confidence or the car make did not agree, so it was refused on purpose.
mistakes.fix: Protect the grills and glass by hand with Region Brush, or use the PSD layers.

protips: A wrong template is treated as worse than none: the engine refuses a template when the folder name advertises a different make than the matched car.
The protect map is feathered with a soft edge (2 px to start) and blended toward the flat finish, so decals fade out of the sculpt instead of being cut with a hard line.

deep.heading: What the detector looks for
deep.body: Auto-detect decals works on a reduced copy of the paint no larger than 768 pixels and combines several cues: edges that stand out, colours that deviate from the base, extreme brightness, glyph strokes of even width (so coloured numbers are found), a repeating grill mesh and small bright clusters inside dark housings. Guards for a busy overall paint, for a patterned base such as carbon, flake or camo, and a cap have the final word, so a busy base is not mistaken for decals. At most 55% of the sheet can be protected, and when the detector is unsure it returns nothing and your whole paint is sculpted.

deep.heading: What protection does to the spec
deep.body: The result is a map where protected pixels are blended toward a flat finish and everything else keeps the sculpt. The blend is softened by a feather of 2 pixels by default. The flat finish is Matte unless you pick another Decal finish: metal 0, roughness 160 and clearcoat 0 for Matte, and roughness 150 for Carbon, 110 for Satin, 45 for Gloss and 35 for Wet. Strength runs from 0.5x to 1.8x in the panel (the engine accepts 0.3x to 2.0x) and starts at 1.0x. A PSD with a layer choice always wins; the auto detector is used only when there is no PSD mask.

examples.title: Default shield on a flat TGA
examples.goal: Keep numbers and sponsors out of the heavy shine.

settings.Preview: click, then read the status line

examples.result: A small image shows what will be protected; build only when the shield sits on the decals and not on the body.

examples.title: Sponsor-heavy car, more eager detection
examples.goal: Catch small sponsor blocks the default misses.

settings.Preview: click and compare with the 1.0x result

examples.result: More small marks are shielded. If body patches turn flat, step the strength back toward 1.0x.

combos.why: The PSD route gives exact control; the auto detector is the quick route for flat paints.
Use Decal Rescue in the booth when a sim-stamped number still sits on chrome after export.
The flat decal finish passes through the same safety pass as the rest of the map.
Preview the shield first, then build and deploy.

faq.q: Is auto-protect on by default?
faq.a: No. Auto-detect decals starts unticked, and it only appears under Advanced.

faq.q: Why did it protect nothing on my camo car?
faq.a: Guards for busy and patterned bases make the detector return nothing rather than guess, so the whole paint is sculpted.

faq.q: Can I change how protected areas look?
faq.a: Yes, with Decal finish: Matte, Satin, Glossy, Wet or Carbon. In this build that picker lives in the PSD layers card, so a flat paint uses the Matte default.

faq.q: Does the Shokk the World gallery respect the shield?
faq.a: Yes. When Auto-detect decals is on, the shield is built once from your paint and reused for every look in the gallery.

mistakes.symptom: Body panels look flat and grey after building.
mistakes.cause: Detect strength is too high, so large body areas were taken for decals (the cap is 55% of the sheet).
mistakes.fix: Lower Detect strength and check the Preview again.

mistakes.symptom: A number is still glossy.
mistakes.cause: It was not detected, often a thin or very low-contrast glyph.
mistakes.fix: Raise Detect strength a little, or protect it with a PSD layer; Decal Rescue in the booth also fixes it after export.

mistakes.symptom: Auto-detect seems ignored on a PSD.
mistakes.cause: A PSD layer selection takes priority over the automatic detector.
mistakes.fix: Untick the layers you want sculpted, or load the flat image if you want the detector instead.

protips: Protection fades in rather than cutting: the feather is a soft Gaussian blur on the mask, so a protected sponsor blends out of the sculpt over a couple of pixels.
Decals that arrive in a real satin or gloss usually read better than dead matte, so try Satin for the Decal finish when you have a PSD.

deep.heading: Drama, Spec strength and the 100% ceiling
deep.body: Drama (0 to 100, starts at 35) is not a separate effect: it sets Spec strength using 50 plus 1.5 times the Drama value, so 0 gives 50% and 100 gives 200%. The label changes at 16 (Balanced), 42 (Bold), 68 (Wild) and 88 (Insane). The build limits the strength multiplier to 100%, which Drama reaches at about 33, so raising Drama beyond that does not add metal. For more punch use Channel trims, a stronger look or a Detail bake. Lower Drama does soften the map, down to half strength.

deep.heading: How Auto-Sculpt picks
deep.body: Auto-Sculpt reads the paint at small size for brightness, saturation, contrast, edges, dark and colourful share, and how bright the centre is. It scores 7 ready-made pairs: Chrome Depth, Candy Show, Dark Satin, Brushed Metal, Anodized Gloss, Machined Graphic and Flake Pop, and builds the best fit. It also sets detail 1.78 when edges are strong (above 0.16), 1.36 when they are low (below 0.08) and 1.59 otherwise, and Interior flatten 44 on dark cars, 36 on bright ones and 38 otherwise. Another Smart Look walks down the ranking. More like this keeps the same looks and nudges each weight by up to 0.10 and the seed, giving 6 close variations.

deep.heading: Housekeeping limits worth knowing
deep.body: Recent keeps your last 8 builds. Compare Looks holds 4 slots; adding a fifth drops the oldest. Batch Sculpt a Folder builds up to 64 files, writes into an output folder that defaults to a spec folder inside the source folder, and treats Fusion, candy and fracture looks as Scratch. Region Brush size runs 6 to 64 (start 24), Snap tolerance 8 to 60 (start 28), and Detail amount starts at 55. Detail bake only changes roughness and clearcoat texture, never the base material, and runs after the protection map. Material Spotlight lights metal where metallic is above 150 and roughness below 95.

faq.q: Can I share a look with a friend?
faq.a: Yes. Copy code makes a short code starting with SHOKK1, and Export makes a portable look file. Saved looks do not store your member ID or car folder.

faq.q: How many looks do Recent and Favorites remember?
faq.a: Recent remembers the last 8. Favorites are pinned until you remove them.

faq.q: What do the keyboard shortcuts do?
faq.a: G or Ctrl+Enter builds, V makes variations, D deploys the last job, W opens Shokk the World, R picks a surprise, and Ctrl+Z with Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo. Press the question mark key for the list.

faq.q: What is Match a Photo?
faq.a: You pick a reference photo of a real surface; the lab reads its gloss, metal and contrast and sculpts your spec to feel like it, copying the finish and not the colours.

mistakes.symptom: Raising Drama to Insane looks the same as Balanced.
mistakes.cause: Drama only sets Spec strength, and the build caps that at 100%.
mistakes.fix: Use the M Channel trim, a bolder look, or Detail bake for extra punch.

mistakes.symptom: A fifth Compare Looks snapshot makes the first one vanish.
mistakes.cause: There are 4 slots and the oldest is replaced.
mistakes.fix: Save the look you want to keep with Save look before adding more.

mistakes.symptom: A folder batch did not apply my candy or FRACTURE look.
mistakes.cause: Batch treats Fusion, candy and fracture looks as Scratch.
mistakes.fix: Use a Scratch or Catalog look for batches, or build those looks one car at a time.

protips: Tap the Eyedropper on your car number and pick a material with everywhere: it makes that colour glossier or more metallic across the whole paint using the same engine as Hue boost.
Series Templates and Theme Packs are one-tap looks tuned to a racing series or a vibe, so they are the quickest start for a new livery.
Saved looks store the blend, detail settings and paint response and are tiny, so keep one for every car family you race.

deep.heading: What the Material readout measures
deep.body: After every preview the lab shrinks the composite to 128 by 128 and counts pixels. Glossy is roughness of 90 or less, metallic is metal of 150 or more, matte is roughness of 175 or more, and a void is a dark, flat pocket with metal of 92 or less and roughness of 158 or more. The bar shows the glossy, metallic and matte shares, scaled to total 100%, and the averages for metal, roughness and clearcoat. Warnings fire when more than 2% of pixels have clearcoat from 1 to 15, more than 80% reads matte, more than 30% is void, or more than 85% reads metallic. With none of those you get Balanced material map.

deep.heading: Iron badge, decorrelation and the time meter
deep.body: The Physically valid badge samples a 160 pixel copy and flags clearcoat from 1 to 15 or roughness under 15 on non-mirror pixels when either covers more than 2%, and a giant chrome plate when more than 55% of pixels have metal of 240 or more. The Channel decorrelation meter measures how much metal, roughness and clearcoat move together: bars are green below 0.6, amber from 0.6 to 0.85 and red above 0.85, and two or more near-constant channels (spread under 6) read as Flat. The render meter turns amber above 2 seconds and red above the 3 second budget. The loupe is on by default and shows a 150 pixel magnified patch with M, R and Cc numbers.

faq.q: Why does the composite preview look pink, lime or orange?
faq.a: Those are false colours: red is metal, green is roughness, blue is clearcoat. Lime or orange means high roughness with moderate metal, which is expected and not a bug.

faq.q: Is the preview the same as the booth swatch colour?
faq.a: No. The composite shows raw channel strength, not how the paint will tint in the sim.

faq.q: What is Material Probe?
faq.a: Click anywhere on the composite to pin a sample point and compare exact M, R and Cc values with a material name across zones. Pins refresh as you re-sculpt.

faq.q: What do the colours of the decorrelation bars mean?
faq.a: Green is independent channels, amber is some overlap, red means metal, roughness and clearcoat move together and the look will read flat on the car.

mistakes.symptom: The readout says clearcoat is in the 1 to 15 band but I fear the file is bad.
mistakes.cause: The preview is shrunk, which can create in-between values; the export snaps them anyway.
mistakes.fix: Build normally: the safety pass makes the final file legal. Raise clearcoat only if you want a stronger coat.

mistakes.symptom: Reading the composite colour as the paint colour.
mistakes.cause: Red, green and blue in the composite mean metal, roughness and clearcoat, not paint hue.
mistakes.fix: Look at the Source paint tile for colour and the channel tiles for each property.

mistakes.symptom: Warning about void pockets after switching to a dark paint.
mistakes.cause: Dark flat areas count as void when metal is 92 or less and roughness is 158 or more.
mistakes.fix: Lower the void caps in Advanced for a paint-derived build, or add a gloss look for contrast.

protips: The dock at the top keeps Source paint, the combined spec and the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat tiles in view while you click through looks, so you can judge each channel without scrolling.
Open How each material looks in iRacing to compare your result with what chrome, candy and matte are expected to look like in the sim.

deep.heading: The three rules as the engine applies them
deep.body: The safety pass has three jobs. Clearcoat: a byte of 1 to 15 is snapped, to 0 if it is under 8 and to 16 otherwise, while an exact 0 stays 0 and everything from 16 up is kept. Roughness: where metal is under 240 the roughness is raised to at least 15, and only true mirror pixels (metal 240 or more) may go lower. Metal: if more than 55% of the car would be mirror metal, those pixels are lowered to 239 so the car is not one giant plate. The map is written as a 32-bit TGA with the lighting mask fully open at 255. The strict 2048 check refuses a wrong size instead of quietly resizing.

deep.heading: Why feathered decals never break the rules
deep.body: Protected decals are blended toward a flat finish with a soft feather, which can create in-between bytes along the edge. The safety pass runs after that blend and after any Detail bake, so those edge values are snapped too: a Matte decal keeps clearcoat at exactly 0 while the sculpted body keeps 16 or more. Look builds also clamp roughness at 15 and clearcoat at 16 as they are made, and the Material Region Brush, Gradient and Color to Material presets keep clearcoat at 18 or more, roughness at 30 or more and metal at 238 or less, so a mix of them cannot go illegal either.

deep.heading: Deploying: ID, car, Live Link and re-deploy
deep.body: The member ID is 4 to 7 digits and sets the file name, so iRacing finds the paint. Deploy to lets you search for your car by name; you can instead paste or browse an exact car folder. Save to the selected car automatically after each Generate (Deploy now) copies after every build. Push via Live Link to your saved active car is the Advanced shortcut for a car you have already set. Deploy last job (no re-render) stays greyed out until a job exists, then copies the last build again without rebuilding. Open folder shows where the files are. A build in Simple mode writes the paint and spec and checks both files.

faq.q: Can I export a clearcoat of 10?
faq.a: Not as 10. Values 1 to 15 are snapped to 0 (under 8) or 16 (8 and up) because that band whitewashes in the sim.

faq.q: Why can my chrome not go fully mirror everywhere?
faq.a: If more than 55% of the car would be mirror metal, the engine lowers those pixels to 239 so the car does not become a single plate.

faq.q: What does the green Physically valid badge mean?
faq.a: The preview passes the iron rules: no clearcoat in 1 to 15, no low roughness on non-mirror pixels, no giant chrome plate. Every build fixes any issue anyway.

faq.q: Do I need the member ID to preview?
faq.a: No. Only deploying and naming the file need it.

mistakes.symptom: Deploy last job is greyed out.
mistakes.cause: No job has been built in this session yet.
mistakes.fix: Click Build spec + iRacing files once, then the button turns on.

mistakes.symptom: The car in iRacing does not change after deploy.
mistakes.cause: Wrong car folder or a member ID that does not match the folder, so iRacing never loads the file.
mistakes.fix: Search Deploy to for your car, check the ID, then refresh the car in iRacing.

mistakes.symptom: A mirror car looks less mirror than the preview thumbnail.
mistakes.cause: More than 55% of the sheet was mirror metal, so those pixels were lowered to 239.
mistakes.fix: Keep mirror finish to the areas that need it and use a satin or matte accent elsewhere.

protips: The exact-0 clearcoat survives only on protected matte decals; every sculpted pixel is 16 or more, which is why decals stay readable over a glossy body.
The lab keeps only the newest 10 jobs, so copy a build you love to another folder or save its look before running many experiments.

deep.heading: Why these five recipes work
deep.body: Each recipe leans on one real behaviour. CANDY DEPTH makes rich and dark areas into deep glassy pools and leaves pale areas as thin satin, so it rewards saturated mid-to-dark paint and reads quiet on white. Chrome rewards dark or mid backgrounds with graphics because the shine contrast shows; and the engine lowers mirror metal to 239 if more than 55% of the sheet would be mirror, so chrome works best as a feature, not a blanket. Carbon and matte win on contrast between a calm body and woven accents. Holo and flake need fine detail, and the Saturated emphasis puts the effect on your colourful areas.

deep.heading: A tuning order that never wastes a build
deep.body: Work in this order. Pick the look first, then protect decals, then adjust the strength with Spec strength or Channel trims, then add a Detail bake last, because it runs after protection. Keep the Seed fixed while you tune, change one setting per build, and use Compare Looks with its 4 slots to judge. When a build is right, save it with Save look; saved looks keep the blend, detail settings and paint response, never your member ID or car, so one good recipe can be reapplied to every livery you race.

faq.q: Where is the one-click version?
faq.a: Wet + pearl and Matte duo are the two quick buttons above the library. Surprise Me and the Style Gallery give other one-tap starts.

faq.q: My candy looks flat on a white car. Why?
faq.a: Candy depth builds deep pools on dark and rich areas. A pale paint stays thin satin, so choose a deeper base colour or raise Depth.

faq.q: Can I use a recipe on another car?
faq.a: Yes. Save look stores the settings and applies them to any livery in one tap.

faq.q: Why do small changes matter so much?
faq.a: Changing the seed changes the random detail and, with no emphasis set, even which part of the paint is emphasised. Keep it fixed while tuning.

mistakes.symptom: The chrome recipe looks dull on a mostly white car.
mistakes.cause: Chrome needs contrast; a bright body gives it little to reflect against in the preview.
mistakes.fix: Add Paint response with Dark panels or pair chrome with a darker accent look.

mistakes.symptom: Every recipe looks the same after I stack extra looks on top.
mistakes.cause: Extra looks of equal weight average out the character of the first one.
mistakes.fix: Keep the recipe to one lead look and small accents, and use Compare Looks to verify.

mistakes.symptom: Detail bake made the decals look worn.
mistakes.cause: Detail runs after the protection map, so it textures protected areas too.
mistakes.fix: Lower Amount from its start of 55 or choose None.

protips: A Matte decal keeps clearcoat at exactly 0 while the body stays at 16 or more, so decals read crisp against a glossy recipe.
To make chrome feel less like a plate, stack a small share of Brushed Titanium under Mirror Chrome: the Brushed Metal auto look uses that very pair.

deep.heading: Region Brush, step by step
deep.body: Pick one of six finishes (Chrome, Wet, Gloss, Satin, Matte, Carbon), set the size from 6 to 64 (starts at 24) and paint on the car. Strokes of the same finish are merged, later strokes win where they overlap, and any pixel you leave unpainted keeps a Satin base. The edge is blurred by 2 pixels. Snap to region (on by default) trims strokes that bleed onto a differently coloured panel; Tol runs 8 to 60 and starts at 28, and lower values snap tighter to the exact colour under the brush. Symmetry can be Off, Vertical (left and right), Horizontal (top and bottom) or Quad. Undo and Clear affect only the brush; Apply brush turns the strokes into a spec preview.

deep.heading: Gradients, edges and Detail bake
deep.body: Material Gradient blends finish A into finish B by position: Horizontal runs left to right, Vertical top to bottom, Diagonal corner to corner, and Radial from the centre outward. Every preset material keeps clearcoat at 18 or more, roughness at 30 or more and metal at 238 or less, so the blend cannot go illegal. Protect edge (grow, from minus 20 to 20, starts at 0) widens the protected halo around logos when positive and lets the sculpt reach closer when negative; the engine limits the change to 64 pixels. Feather runs 0 to 12 (starts at 2). Detail bake offers Swirl marks, Brushed, Micro-scratch, Hairline, Road grime, Orange peel, Water spots, Hammered and Sandblast at an Amount that starts at 55.

examples.title: Chrome front fading to a matte rear
examples.goal: A designed fade across the car.
examples.result: A smooth fade from chrome on one side of the sheet to matte on the other; use Vertical for top to bottom or Radial for a glow.

examples.title: Wider halo around a big logo
examples.goal: Keep sculpt away from a logo edge.
examples.result: The protected area grows by about 6 pixels and its edge softens over a wider band, so the logo has a clean margin.

examples.title: Sandblast on a matte wrap
examples.goal: Fine rough texture without changing the base finish.
examples.result: Roughness and clearcoat pick up a gritty texture while the material underneath is unchanged.

Protect edge, Feather and Decal finish belong to the PSD layer picker.
The booth counterpart for hand-setting materials on a zone.
The same idea of mirroring strokes, applied to the main booth tools.

faq.q: Why does Apply brush say to paint something first?
faq.a: There are no strokes yet. Paint on the car preview, then click Apply brush.

faq.q: What does Snap to region actually do?
faq.a: If you colour a little outside the lines, the stroke is trimmed to the paint region under your brush. Lower Tol makes it trim tighter.

faq.q: Which way does a horizontal gradient run?
faq.a: Finish A is on the left and finish B on the right. Vertical goes top to bottom, and Radial goes from centre to edge.

faq.q: What are the Zone buttons for?
faq.a: Chrome zones, Wet and gloss, Matte zones and Show car light up where each material lives on your car, in plain English.

mistakes.symptom: Brush strokes spill onto the neighbouring panel.
mistakes.cause: Snap to region is off or Tol is too high.
mistakes.fix: Turn Snap to region on and lower Tol toward 8.

mistakes.symptom: Symmetry mirrors onto the wrong place.
mistakes.cause: The sheet is a flat UV layout, so mirroring is about the sheet, not the car body.
mistakes.fix: Use Vertical only when your panels are laid out symmetrically, otherwise paint each side.

mistakes.symptom: Detail bake has no visible effect.
mistakes.cause: Detail is None or Amount is very low.
mistakes.fix: Pick a texture and raise Amount from its start of 55.

protips: Detail bake changes roughness and clearcoat texture only, so it is the safe way to add Hammered or Brushed grain without losing a chrome or candy identity.
Material Spotlight lights where chrome (metal above 150 and roughness under 95), wet gloss and matte live, which is a quick check that a brush or gradient went where you meant.

deep.heading: What each of the four tools touches
deep.body: Material Sampler reads exact M, R, CC and A values from the compiled spec map and can copy them onto the active Zone selection. Lighting Mask edits only the alpha channel of the spec, so paint colours and the metal, roughness and clearcoat channels are untouched. Material Range Remapper changes only metal, roughness and clearcoat inside the active Zone and keeps paint colour and alpha locked. Decal Rescue Kit sets a flat non-metallic spec under numbers and sponsors in the active Zone while keeping the source paint colours. All four act on the active Zone selection only, and one Undo steps back.

deep.heading: Lighting Mask values and Remapper presets
deep.body: Lighting Mask has four choices. Use Source Alpha removes the override and keeps the finish or imported map, Full Lighting sets alpha to 255, Reduced Lighting sets 128 for recessed vents and deep seams, and Kill Lighting sets 0 for fake holes and grille openings; the tool warns it is not a shortcut for matte vinyl. Soft selection edges give a soft alpha transition. The Remapper squeezes each channel into a Low to High range, so source 0 becomes Low, 255 becomes High, and values between scale in proportion. Presets: Metallic Texture metal 205 to 255, roughness 8 to 90, clearcoat 8 to 55; Printed Vinyl metal 0 to 24, roughness 70 to 155, clearcoat 55 to 135; Matte Texture metal 0 to 24, roughness 180 to 255, clearcoat 160 to 230; Gloss Texture metal 0 to 24, roughness 0 to 70, clearcoat 0 to 55.

examples.title: Fix a glassy number on a chrome zone
examples.goal: Make a sim-stamped number readable.

settings.Footprint: draw it with Rectangle, Lasso, Pen or Smart Region, then Mask then Grow

examples.result: Metal 0, roughness 100, clearcoat 110 under the number, so white vinyl reads cleanly over chrome. Satin Decal (clearcoat 75) and Gloss Decal (roughness 42, clearcoat 22) are the softer and shinier options.

examples.title: Calm a wild imported spec map
examples.goal: Keep its texture but narrow its range.
examples.result: Metal 0 to 24, roughness 70 to 155 and clearcoat 55 to 135, with scratches, weave and flake kept. Restore Original undoes it.

examples.title: A recessed vent that looks unlit
examples.goal: Make a vent sit deeper without painting it black.
examples.result: The vent footprint gets alpha 128, half-strength lighting, for a recessed look; Kill Lighting (alpha 0) is only for true cutouts.

combos.why: The full explanation of how these three tools sit in the spec pipeline.
Lighting Mask is the alpha channel; read this for what alpha does in iRacing.
Decal Rescue from the layer side, with the same three presets.
The separate lab builds a whole spec map; these tools fine-tune one zone.

faq.q: Where is the Spec Tools menu?
faq.a: In the top bar of the booth, next to the Mask menu. It lists Decal Rescue Kit, Lighting Mask, Material Sampler and Range Remapper.

faq.q: Does the Lighting Mask change colour or shine?
faq.a: No. It only controls how much sun, reflection and environment lighting reaches the footprint, through the alpha channel.

faq.q: What does Restore Original do in the Remapper?
faq.a: It returns the zone to its original material ranges; the Original preset is the full 0 to 255 range for every channel.

faq.q: Do these tools change my paint?
faq.a: No. Paint colours stay locked in all four tools.

mistakes.symptom: A matte panel was made with Kill Lighting and now looks like a hole.
mistakes.cause: Kill Lighting sets alpha 0 and suppresses spec and environment light entirely.
mistakes.fix: Use Reduced Lighting for depth or a matte finish for flat vinyl; keep Kill Lighting for true cutouts.

mistakes.symptom: Remapper made the texture disappear.
mistakes.cause: A very narrow range squeezes all variation into nearly one value.
mistakes.fix: Widen Low and High, or pick a preset such as Printed Vinyl and press Apply Remap again.

mistakes.symptom: Decal Rescue changed more than the number.
mistakes.cause: The footprint covered more than the stamp.
mistakes.fix: Draw a tighter footprint and use Mask then Grow only enough to cover the edge.

protips: Applying a remap clears a flat Material Sampler override on the zone so the retained texture is visible; the Lighting Mask alpha stays separate and untouched.
Decal Rescue is Zone-only and keeps source colours locked, so you can use it after every other design decision without redoing the paint.
